speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I see you are presenting with a chronic wound on your right lower leg; could you tell me how long you have had this wound and how it appeared initially?

speaker: Patient
text: 57-year-old male. The patient reports a large wound on his right lower leg that has been present for 6 months. He mentions that his legs have been chronically swollen for over 10 years and that his mother and brother had similar leg problems. He had a documented deep vein thrombosis (DVT) in the affected leg 5 years ago but has no other significant past medical history.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for those details. Given your history of chronic swelling, a past DVT, and the family history suggesting a possible venous or lymphatic disorder, have you noticed any varicose veins, skin discoloration, or thickening around the wound site?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Large wound on the right lower leg. I also have Chronic leg swelling, Family history of similar leg problems.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Chronic Venous Insufficiency with Stasis Ulcer

The combination of chronic leg swelling, a history of DVT, family history, and a non-healing lower leg wound strongly points to this diagnosis. I will now request a Venous Doppler Ultrasound to confirm venous insufficiency and assess for any active reflux or residual thrombosis.
